claims.text: Renal failure: calcitriol (or another analog that needs no renal activation);
claims.quote: For patients with renal failure, calcitriol or another vitamin D analog that does not require renal metabolic alteration (eg, alfacalcidiol, dihydrotachysterol) should be used.

claims.text: hypoparathyroidism: often needs calcitriol 0.5 to 2 mcg PO daily (can't activate cholecalciferol)
claims.quote: Patients with hypoparathyroidism also have difficulty converting cholecalciferol to its active form and also often require calcitriol, usually 0.5 to 2 mcg orally once a day.

claims.text: W hypomagnesemia: tetany is permanently relieved only by Mg (10% magnesium sulfate IV, then oral Mg salts)
claims.quote: When hypocalcemic tetany is also associated with hypomagnesemia, it may respond transiently to calcium or potassium administration but is permanently relieved only by repletion of magnesium, typically given as a 10% magnesium sulfate solution (1 g/10 mL) IV, followed by oral magnesium salts
